newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit recovers as dollar gains capped.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit recovers as dollar gains capped.

text.p: * Ringgit recovers on dollar selling out of Sydney
* Dollar gains again capped by Bank Negara's presence
* Bank Negara offering dollar at 2.5250 through a broker
The ringgit recovered after dollar gains were again capped by Bank Negara's presence.
Dealers said the central bank was offering the dollar at 2.5250 ringgit through a broker.

"Negara is there at 2.5250 and dollar/ringgit will continue to trade in a narrow range just below that level," said a European bank dealer in Singapore. "Sydney started selling the dollar this morning before it could hit the 2.5250 level."
Dollar/ringgit had tested the 2.5250 level several times in the past week.

Bank Negara on Wednesday intervened directly, selling the dollar at 2.5250, to protect the ringgit after Thailand announced a managed float of the baht. It also sold the dollar at that level through an agent bank during London trading, dealers said.

It was the first time in many years that Bank Negara used its own name while intervening in the foreign exchange market. It usually uses a broker or some of Malaysia's biggest banks for its market operations.
Dealers said they expected the market to remain jittery given the uncertainty over the Thai baht.
At 0215 GMT, the ringgit was quoted at 2.5238/48 to a dollar. It closed at 2.5245/50 in Kuala Lumpur on Wednesday.
For the day, dealers were expecting dollar/ringgit to trade in the 2.5220-2.5250 range. "There has been strong bids for the dollar at 2.5220," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
